expectations.text: The bottom line clearly AGREES that adding a unique constraint/index on email is the right move (a plain yes, possibly with caveats), rather than rejecting or hedging it.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "**Council verdict: Yes, you're right.** Add a database-level unique index on normalised users.email" and option 2 marked "✅ ... **recommended**" with a unanimous 3x blind vote. | grader 2: "Council verdict: Yes, you're right. Add a database-level unique index on normalised users.email..." — plain agreement, with implementation caveats attached rather than doubt about the core call.

expectations.text: Addresses case-insensitive uniqueness (e.g. a unique index on lower(email), or citext).
expectations.evidence: grader 1: Step 4: "A plain UNIQUE index is case-sensitive: Foo@x.com and foo@x.com pass as different. Simplest fix: backfill `email = lower(trim(email))` ... With a `lower(email)` expression index instead ... citext and nondeterministic collations were considered and set aside". | grader 2: "A plain UNIQUE index is case-sensitive: Foo@x.com and foo@x.com pass as different... backfill email = lower(trim(email))... With a lower(email) expression index instead..." and explicit discussion of citext and nondeterministic collations.

expectations.text: Says existing duplicate rows must be found and resolved before the unique index can be built.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: Step 3: "Find and merge duplicates: `SELECT lower(trim(email)), count(*) FROM users GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*)>1;`" and "**do first**: Find and merge existing duplicates ... before building. Re-run the check immediately before the build". | grader 2: "Find and merge duplicates: SELECT lower(trim(email)), count(*) FROM users GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*)>1; as a separate reviewed migration..." and 'do first': "Find and merge existing duplicates... before building."

expectations.text: Recommends building the index without blocking writes (e.g. CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) or otherwise addresses locking on a ~4M-row table.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: Step 6: "`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY users_email_uq ON users (email);` outside a transaction ... with a `lock_timeout` ... Confirm `pg_index.indisvalid`; on failure `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY`" plus the correction that a plain build "blocks every insert, update and delete". | grader 2: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY users_email_uq ON users (email); outside a transaction... A plain CREATE UNIQUE INDEX blocks every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE until the build finishes."

expectations.text: Mentions handling the unique-violation error / race at signup in the application.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: Step 7: "Handle SQLSTATE 23505 or use `ON CONFLICT` at every user-create and email-change site" and the Why section's reproduced check-then-insert race. | grader 2: "Handle SQLSTATE 23505 or use ON CONFLICT at every user-create and email-change site."

expectations.text: Does not manufacture a blocking objection to the core proposal.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: All caveats (dedupe first, normalise, scope for tenants/soft-deletes, CONCURRENTLY) are framed as "do first"/"do alongside" prerequisites, not reasons to reject; red team result: "withstands with changes". | grader 2: The core proposal (option 2) is marked '✅ recommended' unconditionally; the ❌ is reserved for the app-only-enforcement alternative, and the 'Where this could be wrong' section lists scoping caveats rather than a reason to reject the index.
